The auction will be conducted on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system on October 27, 2026 (Tuesday). The Government Stock up to ten per cent of the notified amount of the sale of each stock will be allotted to eligible individuals and institutions, subject to a maximum limit of one per cent of its notified amount for a single bid per stock as per the ‘Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility’. Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).

Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system on October 27, 2026 (Tuesday). The competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 A.M. and 11:30 A.M. and non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 A.M. and 11:00 A.M.

In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team may be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).

For other auction related difficulties, IDMD Auction Team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).

Only in the event of system failure, physical bids would be accepted. Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form obtainable from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.

The yield per cent per annum or the price as the case may be, expected by the bidder should be expressed up to two decimal points. An investor can submit more than one competitive bid at same/different rates of yield or prices in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system. However, the aggregate amount of bids submitted by a bidder should not exceed the notified amount for each State.

The Reserve Bank of India will determine the maximum yield / minimum price at which bids will be accepted. Stock will be issued for a minimum nominal amount of ₹10,000.00 and in multiples of ₹10,000.00 thereafter.

The results of the auction will be announced on October 27, 2026 (Tuesday) and payment by successful bidders will be made during banking hours on October 28, 2026 (Wednesday) at Mumbai and at respective Regional Offices of RBI.

The new State Government Stocks will bear interest at the rates determined by RBI at the auctions. For the new stock, interest will be paid half yearly on April 28 and October 28 of each year till maturity. For the re-issued Government Stock, interest will be paid at the rate as determined on the date of original issue of Government Stock and will be paid on half yearly basis till maturity. The Stocks will be governed by the provisions of the Government Securities Act, 2006 and the Government Securities Regulations, 2007.

The investment in State Government Stocks will be reckoned as an eligible investment in Government Securities by banks for the purpose of Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. The stocks will qualify for the ready forward facility.

Ajit Prasad           
Deputy General Manager

item.title: RBI Bulletin – October 2026
item.description:
Today, the Reserve Bank released the October 2026 issue of its monthly Bulletin. The Bulletin includes two speeches, four articles and current statistics.

The four articles are: I. State of the Economy; II. Transmission to Lending Rates of SCBs: Price versus Composition Effects in WALR; III. Performance of the NBFC Sector: Review for 2025; and IV. Nowcasting State-Level Economic Activity in India with Night-Time Light and Google Trends.

I. State of the Economy

Renewed geopolitical frictions in West Asia and supply chain disruptions have amplified inflationary pressures, prompting major central banks to raise policy rates. Elevated sovereign bond yields in advanced economies (AEs) have also brought into focus concerns about fiscal sustainability and its implications for financial stability. The Indian economy continued to demonstrate strength as evidenced by high-frequency indicators across both industry and services. The headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation edged up in September driven by a broad-based increase in food, fuel, and core components. Double-digit growth in merchandise exports during the first six months of 2026-27 helped in narrowing the trade deficit. FDI, ECB and remittance flows strengthened in August. Strong inflows under the FCNR(B) swap window augmented reserves.

II. Transmission to Lending Rates of SCBs: Price versus Composition Effects in WALR

By Yuvraj Kashyap, Kamal Gupta and Arvind Jha

This article analyses the transmission of monetary policy to the fresh lending rates of scheduled commercial banks by decomposing variations in the weighted average lending rate (WALR) into interest rate effects and compositional effects. Using an index-number based framework on bank and sector level lending rates and loan weights, the study examines the extent to which changes in the aggregate WALR reflect changes in lending rates and shifts in credit composition.

Highlights:

  • In response to a cumulative reduction of 125 basis points (bps) in the policy repo rate, the WALR on fresh lending declined by 93 bps, with interest rate effect of 80 bps and composition effect of 13 bps during February 2025 to March 2026.

  • The movements in aggregate WALR reflect both repricing of loans and changes in the composition of credit across banks and sectors, highlighting the importance of both effects while assessing monetary policy transmission.

III. Performance of the NBFC Sector: Review for 2025

By Pallavi Pant, Monalisa Poali, Abhyuday Harsh, Brijesh P and Sona Chinngaihlian

This article assesses the performance of the non-banking financial company (NBFC) sector up to end-December 2025. It also provides a bird’s-eye-view of India’s financial system. Employing a text-mining approach, the article also explores the extent and nature of orientation towards artificial intelligence (AI) by select NBFCs.

Highlights:

  • The NBFC sector continued to register double-digit y-o-y credit growth at end-December 2025.

  • Share of bank borrowings showed a moderate rise indicating continued concentration in funding profile. Asset quality of the sector has continued to improve in recent years as reflected in consistent decline in NPA ratios.

  • Preliminary text-mining analysis shows that NBFCs are increasingly orienting towards AI for customer and financial applications, governance and digital infrastructure, and data analytics.

IV. Nowcasting State-Level Economic Activity in India with Night-Time Light and Google Trends

By Bipul Ghosh, Narendra Singh and Sandhya Kuruganti

Timely measurement of state-level economic activity remains a challenge in India, as official Gross State Value Added (GSVA) data are released annually with a considerable lag. This study demonstrates how alternative data sources, specifically satellite-based night-time lights and digital search behaviour, can be used to generate high-frequency estimates of state-level economic activity. The framework is applied to three major states — Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. It shows how combining geospatial and behavioural signals can provide a real-time view of regional economic dynamics and strengthen short-term economic assessment.

Highlights:

  • The combined use of night-time lights and Google Trends improves nowcast accuracy of quarterly GSVA growth relative to univariate approach.

  • The approach enables near real-time monitoring of state-level economies, improving early detection of turning points and shocks.

  • The methodology is scalable and demonstrates the potential of alternative data in supplementing official statistical systems and high-frequency macroeconomic analysis.

The views expressed in the Bulletin articles are those of the authors and do not represent the views of the Reserve Bank of India.

(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager

item.title: RBI issues Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Forthcoming Instructions) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 on Minimum Capital Requirements for Operational Risk
item.description:
The Reserve Bank of India had issued Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Forthcoming Instructions) Directions, 2025 on November 28, 2025.

2. Chapter IV of these Directions prescribed the Minimum Capital Requirements for Operational Risk, wherein it was specified that the effective date of implementation and indicative mapping of the components of the Business Indicator (BI) to the schedules and line items of the financial statements shall be provided in due course. Subsequently, Governor in his Statement dated October 01, 2025, announced that the revised Basel III capital adequacy framework for Commercial Banks (excluding Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Payment Banks (PBs), Regional Rural Banks(RRBs)) would come into effect from April 01, 2027. Further, post issuance of these Directions, certain additional clarifications have been issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.

3. In view of the above developments, the Reserve Bank has today released the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Forthcoming Instructions) Second Amendment Directions, 2026, specifying the implementation date for the new Standardised Approach (‘Basel III Standardised Approach’ or ‘Basel III SA’) for minimum operational risk regulatory capital requirements, providing an indicative mapping of BI components, and incorporating additional clarifications.

(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager

item.title: RBI issues guidelines on the implementation of Leverage Ratio 2017 Standard
item.description:
The Reserve Bank of India had issued the draft Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Eleventh Amendment Directions, 2026 on August 7, 2026, inviting feedback from stakeholders until August 28, 2026. The draft Amendment Directions proposed to implement the latest leverage ratio framework ('Leverage Ratio 2017 Standard') issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.

2. Feedback received on the draft Directions has been examined and consequent modifications have been suitably incorporated in the final Amendment Directions. The statement on the feedback received on the draft Directions is provided in the Annex.

3. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank has today released the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Eleventh Amendment Directions, 2026.

4. These instructions will come into effect from April 1, 2027.

(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager
